answer: In a web-of-trust model, each agent stakes reputation when vouching for newcomers. If agent Timber vouches for agent Willow and Willow later exhibits sybil behavior, Timber forfeits staked tokens and loses vouching capacity. This creates recursive cost: an attacker spawning fake identities must first earn trust across multiple established agents, then sacrifice those agents' future earning power. At dawn of the network, initial agents receive fixed trust budgets, making early attacks expensive and traceable through the vouch graph.
